complete_examples.text: As to the wheel–rail interaction at 3D space, the wheel– rail nonlinear contact forces can be respectively, charac-terized by Hertzian theory in normal contact (Hertz, 1896) and by creep theory with saturation modification in tan-gential contact (Kalker, 1967; Shen et al., 1983), which has been condensed to be a wheel–rail spatially coupling model with high accuracy and efficiency in the work of Zhai et al. (2009).

Different from other high-efficient techniques, for example, the 2.5D finite element method (Yang and Hung, 2001) and the periodic finite element model (Degrande et al., 2006), the hybrid model can describe the complex wheel-rail nonlinear contact behavior by the nonlinear Hertz contact and the creep theory.
